cards.note: Verse 9's fourth and fifth sentences, both stated for the identical "own country" verdict ("the same will happen when...") and encoded together as one card's own two-branch disjunction rather than split, matching the way this store already treats one book-given name/one effect covering several named mechanisms (e.g. PD.07.Neechabhanga.LordOrExaltedInSign's own five-way "any"). Sentence one: "the sign" is the 10th house's own sign (subject of the two sentences immediately before, both about "the sign representing the 10th house"); "its lord" is that sign's ruling graha, i.e. the 10th house's own lord -- lord_of_house(?g,10) AND (in_house(?g,10) [occupied] OR aspects(?g,target=10) [aspected]); aspects already emits graha-to-house facts (full drishti onto a house number, not only onto another graha -- dep.aspects, Engine/facts.py::_aspects), so no new predicate is needed. Sentence two: "a fixed sign" is read against the same per-sign mobility table PD.01.SignAttributes.* (ch.1) already carries (Doctrine.sign_attributes(sign)["mobility"]) -- of the seven Navamsa-owner sign pairs vv.2-8 (PD.05.Livelihood.*) already use, exactly four individual signs are "Fixed": Leo (Sun), Taurus (one of Venus's two), Scorpio (one of Mars's two) and Aquarius (one of Saturn's two) -- Mercury's and Jupiter's own pairs are both Dual, Moon's and the other halves of Mars/Venus/Saturn's are Moveable, so neither is ever satisfiable and correctly contributes no branch. Sign mobility is chart-independent doctrine (Aries is always Moveable), so this is authoring-time embedding exactly like vv.2-8's own Navamsa sign-lord table, not a new predicate: in_sign_class (dep.sign-class) turns out to be both already implemented AND the wrong shape for this clause regardless (it classifies a graha's own Rasi sign, not a divisional placement) -- see dep.sign-class's own corrected entry in Rules/deferred.json. Both branches guarded by the same drift-guard regression test as vv.2-8's own table (Engine/tests/test_chapter_five_livelihood.py). The verse's own first sentence (which country, by name, a given sign or Navamsa indicates) and its closing sentence (the mirror-image "other than its lord" foreign-country clause, needing a graha-distinct-from-?g quantifier the condition language does not have) are deferred separately -- see passage:phaladeepika.05.p022-country-general and passage:phaladeepika.05.p022-foreign.
